184|    def get_passthrough_base(type: Any) -> Any:
185|        return get_type_alias_base(type) if is_type_alias(type) else type
186|
187|    args = {get_passthrough_base(type) for type in union.__args__}
188|
189|    def make_structure_native_union(exact_type: Any) -> Callable:
190|        # `exact_type` is likely to be a subset of the entire configured union (`args`).
191|        literal_values = {
192|            v for t in exact_type.__args__ if is_literal(t) for v in t.__args__
193|        }
194|
195|        # We have no idea what the actual type of `val` will be, so we can't
196|        # use it blindly with an `in` check since it might not be hashable.
197|        # So we do an additional check when handling literals.
198|        # Note: do no use `literal_values` here, since {0, False} gets reduced to {0}
199|        literal_classes = {
200|            v.__class__
201|            for t in exact_type.__args__
202|            if is_literal(t)
203|            for v in t.__args__
204|        }
205|
206|        non_literal_classes = {
207|            get_newtype_base(t) or get_passthrough_base(t)
208|            for t in exact_type.__args__
209|            if not is_literal(t)
210|            and ((get_newtype_base(t) or get_passthrough_base(t)) in args)
211|        }
212|
213|        # We augment the set of allowed classes with any configured subclasses of
214|        # the exact subclasses.
215|        non_literal_classes |= {
216|            a for a in args if any(is_subclass(a, c) for c in non_literal_classes)
217|        }
218|
219|        # We check for spillover - union types not handled by the strategy.
220|        # If spillover exists and we fail to validate our types, we call
221|        # further into the converter with the rest.
222|        spillover = {
223|            a
224|            for a in exact_type.__args__
225|            if (get_newtype_base(a) or get_passthrough_base(a))
226|            not in non_literal_classes

231|        if (
232|            accept_ints_as_floats

234|            and float in args
235|            and float in non_literal_classes
236|            and int not in non_literal_classes

238|            non_literal_classes.add(int)

240|        if spillover:
241|            spillover_type = (
242|                Union[tuple(spillover)] if len(spillover) > 1 else next(iter(spillover))
243|            )

245|            def structure_native_union(
246|                val: Any,
247|                _: Any,
248|                classes=non_literal_classes,
249|                vals=literal_values,
250|                converter=converter,
251|                spillover=spillover_type,

253|                if val.__class__ in literal_classes and val in vals:

255|                if val.__class__ in classes:

291|                get_newtype_base(t) or get_passthrough_base(t)
292|                for t in type_args

32|    return bool(actual & given)

35|def _get_union_type(cl: type, given_subclasses_tree: tuple[type]) -> type | None:
36|    actual_subclass_tree = tuple(_make_subclasses_tree(cl))
37|    class_tree = tuple(set(actual_subclass_tree) & set(given_subclasses_tree))
38|    return Union[class_tree] if len(class_tree) >= 2 else None

43|
44|def include_subclasses(
45|    cl: type,
46|    converter: C,
47|    subclasses: tuple[type, ...] | None = None,
48|    union_strategy: Callable[[Any, C], Any] | None = None,
49|    overrides: dict[str, AttributeOverride] | None = None,
50|) -> None:
51|    """
52|    Configure the converter so that the attrs/dataclass `cl` is un/structured as if it
53|    was a union of itself and all its subclasses that are defined at the time when this
54|    strategy is applied.
55|
56|    :param cl: A base `attrs` or `dataclass` class.
57|    :param converter: The `Converter` on which this strategy is applied. Do note that
58|        the strategy does not work for a :class:`cattrs.BaseConverter`.
59|    :param subclasses: A tuple of subclasses whose ancestor is `cl`. If left as `None`,
60|        subclasses are detected using recursively the `__subclasses__` method of `cl`
61|        and its descendents.
62|    :param union_strategy: A callable of two arguments passed by position
63|        (`subclass_union`, `converter`) that defines the union strategy to use to
64|        disambiguate the subclasses union. If `None` (the default), the automatic unique
65|        field disambiguation is used which means that every single subclass
66|        participating in the union must have an attribute name that does not exist in
67|        any other sibling class.
68|    :param overrides: a mapping of `cl` attribute names to overrides (instantiated with
69|        :func:`cattrs.gen.override`) to customize un/structuring.
70|
71|    .. versionadded:: 23.1.0
72|    .. versionchanged:: 24.1.0
73|       When overrides are not provided, hooks for individual classes are retrieved from
74|       the converter instead of generated with no overrides, using converter defaults.
75|    .. versionchanged:: 25.2.0
76|       Slotted dataclasses work on Python 3.14 via :func:`cattrs.subclasses.subclasses`,
77|       which filters out duplicate classes caused by slotting.
78|    """
79|    # Due to https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/1047
80|    collect()
81|    if subclasses is not None:
82|        parent_subclass_tree = (cl, *subclasses)
83|    else:
84|        parent_subclass_tree = tuple(_make_subclasses_tree(cl))
85|
86|    if union_strategy is None:
87|        _include_subclasses_without_union_strategy(
88|            cl, converter, parent_subclass_tree, overrides
89|        )
90|    else:
91|        _include_subclasses_with_union_strategy(
92|            converter, parent_subclass_tree, union_strategy, overrides
93|        )
94|
95|
96|def _include_subclasses_without_union_strategy(
97|    cl,
98|    converter: BaseConverter,
99|    parent_subclass_tree: tuple[type, ...],
100|    overrides: dict[str, AttributeOverride] | None,
101|):
102|    # The iteration approach is required if subclasses are more than one level deep:
103|    for cl in parent_subclass_tree:
104|        # We re-create a reduced union type to handle the following case:
105|        #
106|        #     converter.structure(d, as=Child)
107|        #
108|        # In the above, the `as=Child` argument will be transformed to a union type of
109|        # itself and its subtypes, that way we guarantee that the returned object will
110|        # not be the parent.
111|        subclass_union = _get_union_type(cl, parent_subclass_tree)
112|
113|        def cls_is_cl(cls, _cl=cl):
114|            return cls is _cl
115|
116|        if overrides is not None:
117|            base_struct_hook = make_dict_structure_fn(cl, converter, **overrides)
118|            base_unstruct_hook = make_dict_unstructure_fn(cl, converter, **overrides)
119|        else:
120|            base_struct_hook = converter.get_structure_hook(cl)
121|            base_unstruct_hook = converter.get_unstructure_hook(cl)
122|
123|        if subclass_union is None:
124|
125|            def struct_hook(val: dict, _, _cl=cl, _base_hook=base_struct_hook) -> cl:
126|                return _base_hook(val, _cl)
127|
128|        else:
129|            dis_fn = converter._get_dis_func(subclass_union, overrides=overrides)
130|
131|            def struct_hook(
132|                val: dict,
133|                _,
134|                _c=converter,
135|                _cl=cl,
136|                _base_hook=base_struct_hook,
137|                _dis_fn=dis_fn,
138|            ) -> cl:
139|                """
140|                If val is disambiguated to the class `cl`, use its base hook.
141|
142|                If val is disambiguated to a subclass, dispatch on its exact runtime
143|                type.
144|                """
145|                dis_cl = _dis_fn(val)
146|                if dis_cl is _cl:
147|                    return _base_hook(val, _cl)
148|                return _c.structure(val, dis_cl)
149|
150|        def unstruct_hook(
151|            val: parent_subclass_tree[0],
152|            _c=converter,
153|            _cl=cl,
154|            _base_hook=base_unstruct_hook,
155|        ) -> dict:
156|            """
157|            If val is an instance of the class `cl`, use the hook.
158|
159|            If val is an instance of a subclass, dispatch on its exact runtime type.
160|            """
161|            if val.__class__ is _cl:
162|                return _base_hook(val)
163|            return _c.unstructure(val, unstructure_as=val.__class__)
164|
165|        # This needs to use function dispatch, using singledispatch will again
166|        # match A and all subclasses, which is not what we want.
167|        converter.register_structure_hook_func(cls_is_cl, struct_hook)
168|        converter.register_unstructure_hook_func(cls_is_cl, unstruct_hook)
169|
170|
171|def _include_subclasses_with_union_strategy(
172|    converter: C,
173|    union_classes: tuple[type, ...],
174|    union_strategy: Callable[[Any, C], Any],
175|    overrides: dict[str, AttributeOverride] | None,
176|):
177|    """
178|    This function is tricky because we're dealing with what is essentially a circular
179|    reference.
180|
181|    We need to generate a structure hook for a class that is both:
182|    * specific for that particular class and its own fields
183|    * but should handle specific functions for all its descendants too
184|
185|    Hence the dance with registering below.
186|    """
187|
188|    parent_classes = [cl for cl in union_classes if _has_subclasses(cl, union_classes)]
189|    if not parent_classes:
190|        return
191|
192|    original_unstruct_hooks = {}
193|    original_struct_hooks = {}
194|
195|    original_working_set = None
196|    if hasattr(already_generating, "working_set"):
197|        original_working_set = already_generating.working_set.copy()
198|
199|    for cl in union_classes:
200|        # In the first pass, every class gets its own unstructure function according to
201|        # the overrides.
202|        # We just generate the hooks, and do not register them. This allows us to
203|        # manipulate the _already_generating set to force runtime dispatch.
204|        already_generating.working_set = set(union_classes) - {cl}
205|        try:
206|            if overrides is not None:
207|                unstruct_hook = make_dict_unstructure_fn(cl, converter, **overrides)
208|                struct_hook = make_dict_structure_fn(cl, converter, **overrides)
209|            else:
210|                unstruct_hook = converter.get_unstructure_hook(cl, cache_result=False)
211|                struct_hook = converter.get_structure_hook(cl, cache_result=False)
212|        finally:
213|            already_generating.working_set = set()
214|        original_unstruct_hooks[cl] = unstruct_hook
215|        original_struct_hooks[cl] = struct_hook
216|
217|    if original_working_set is not None:
218|        already_generating.working_set = original_working_set
219|
220|    # Now that's done, we can register all the hooks and generate the
221|    # union handler. The union handler needs them.
222|    final_union = Union[union_classes]  # type: ignore
223|
224|    for cl, hook in original_unstruct_hooks.items():
225|
226|        def cls_is_cl(cls, _cl=cl):
227|            return cls is _cl
228|
229|        converter.register_unstructure_hook_func(cls_is_cl, hook)
230|
231|    for cl, hook in original_struct_hooks.items():
232|
233|        def cls_is_cl(cls, _cl=cl):
234|            return cls is _cl
235|
236|        converter.register_structure_hook_func(cls_is_cl, hook)
237|
238|    union_strategy(final_union, converter)
239|    unstruct_hook = converter.get_unstructure_hook(final_union)
240|    struct_hook = converter.get_structure_hook(final_union)
241|
242|    for cl in union_classes:
243|        # In the second pass, we overwrite the hooks with the union hook.
244|
245|        def cls_is_cl(cls, _cl=cl):
246|            return cls is _cl
247|
248|        converter.register_unstructure_hook_func(cls_is_cl, unstruct_hook)
249|        subclasses = tuple(
250|            [
251|                c
252|                for c in union_classes
253|                if issubclass(typing.get_origin(c) or c, typing.get_origin(cl) or cl)
254|            ]
255|        )
256|        if len(subclasses) > 1:
257|            u = Union[subclasses]  # type: ignore
258|            union_strategy(u, converter)
259|            struct_hook = converter.get_structure_hook(u)
260|
261|            def sh(payload: dict, _, _u=u, _s=struct_hook) -> cl:
262|                return _s(payload, _u)
263|
264|            converter.register_structure_hook_func(cls_is_cl, sh)

1|# Built-in Hooks
2|
3|```{currentmodule} cattrs
4|```
5|
6|_cattrs_ converters come with with a large repertoire of un/structuring hooks built-in.
7|As always, complex hooks compose with simpler ones.
8|
9|## Primitive Values
10|
11|### `int`, `float`, `str`, `bytes`
12|
13|When structuring, use any of these types to coerce the object to that type.
14|
15|```{doctest}
16|
17|>>> cattrs.structure(1, str)
18|'1'
19|>>> cattrs.structure("1", float)
20|1.0
21|```
22|
23|In case the conversion isn't possible the expected exceptions will be propagated out.
24|The particular exceptions are the same as if you'd tried to do the coercion directly.
25|
26|```python
27|>>> cattrs.structure("not-an-int", int)
28|Traceback (most recent call last):
29|...
30|ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'not-an-int'
31|```
32|
33|Coercion is performed for performance and compatibility reasons.
34|Any of these hooks can be overriden if pure validation is required instead.
35|
36|```{doctest}
37|>>> c = Converter()
38|
39|>>> @c.register_structure_hook
40|... def validate(value, type) -> int:
41|...     if not isinstance(value, type):
42|...         raise ValueError(f'{value!r} not an instance of {type}')
43|...     return value
44|
45|>>> c.structure("1", int)
46|Traceback (most recent call last):
47|...
48|ValueError: '1' not an instance of <class 'int'>
49|```
50|
51|When unstructuring, these types are passed through unchanged.
52|
53|### Enums
54|
55|Enums are structured by their values, and unstructured to their values.
56|
57|```{doctest}
58|
59|>>> @unique
60|... class CatBreed(Enum):
61|...    SIAMESE = "siamese"
62|...    MAINE_COON = "maine_coon"
63|...    SACRED_BIRMAN = "birman"
64|
65|>>> cattrs.structure("siamese", CatBreed)
66|<CatBreed.SIAMESE: 'siamese'>
67|
68|>>> cattrs.unstructure(CatBreed.SIAMESE)
69|'siamese'
70|```
71|
72|Enum structuring and unstructuring even works for complex values, like tuples, but if you have anything but simple literal types in those tuples (`str`, `bool`, `int`, `float`) you should consider defining the Enum value's type via the `_value_` attribute's type hint so that cattrs can properly structure it. See [the Python typing documentation](https://typing.python.org/en/latest/spec/enums.html#member-values) for more information on this type hint.
73|
74|```{doctest}
75|
76|>>> @unique
77|... class VideoStandard(Enum):
78|...    NTSC = "ntsc"
79|...    PAL = "pal"
80|
81|>>> @unique
82|... class Resolution(Enum):
83|...     _value_: tuple[VideoStandard, int]
84|...     NTSC_0 = (VideoStandard.NTSC, 0)
85|...     PAL_0 = (VideoStandard.PAL, 0)
86|...     NTSC_1 = (VideoStandard.NTSC, 1)
87|...     PAL_1 = (VideoStandard.PAL, 1)
88|
89|>>> cattrs.structure(("ntsc", 1), Resolution)
90|<Resolution.NTSC_1: (<VideoStandard.NTSC: 'ntsc'>, 1)>
91|
92|>>> cattrs.unstructure(Resolution.PAL_0)
93|['pal', 0]
94|```
95|
96|Again, in case of errors, the expected exceptions are raised.
97|
98|### `pathlib.Path`
99|
100|[`pathlib.Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) objects are structured using their string value,
101|and unstructured into their string value.
102|
103|```{doctest}
104|>>> from pathlib import Path
105|
106|>>> cattrs.structure("/root", Path)
107|PosixPath('/root')
108|
109|>>> cattrs.unstructure(Path("/root"))
110|'/root'
111|```
112|
113|In case the conversion isn't possible, the resulting exception is propagated out.
114|
115|```{versionadded} 23.1.0
116|
117|```
118|
119|
120|## Collections and Related Generics
121|
122|
123|### Optionals
124|
125|`Optional` primitives and collections are supported out of the box.
126|[PEP 604](https://peps.python.org/pep-0604/) optionals (`T | None`) are also supported on Python 3.10 and later.
127|
128|```{doctest}
129|
130|>>> cattrs.structure(None, int)
131|Traceback (most recent call last):
132|...
133|TypeError: int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a number, not 'NoneType'
134|
135|>>> print(cattrs.structure(None, int | None))
136|None
137|```
138|
139|Bare `Optional` s (non-parameterized, just `Optional`, as opposed to `Optional[str]`) aren't supported; `Optional[Any]` should be used instead.
140|
141|`Optionals` handling can be customized using {meth}`register_structure_hook` and {meth}`register_unstructure_hook`.
142|
143|```{doctest}
144|>>> converter = Converter()
145|
146|>>> @converter.register_structure_hook
147|... def hook(val: Any, type: Any) -> str | None:
148|...     if val in ("", None):
149|...         return None
150|...     return str(val)
151|...
152|
153|>>> print(converter.structure("", str | None))
154|None
155|```
156|
157|
158|### Lists
159|
160|Lists can be structured from any iterable object.
161|Types converting to lists are:
162|
163|- `collections.abc.MutableSequence[T]`
164|- `typing.List[T]`
165|- `list[T]`
166|
167|In all cases, a new list will be returned, so this operation can be used to copy an iterable into a list.
168|A bare type, for example `Sequence` instead of `Sequence[int]`, is equivalent to `Sequence[Any]`.
169|
170|```{doctest}
171|
172|>>> cattrs.structure((1, 2, 3), MutableSequence[int])
173|[1, 2, 3]
174|```
175|
176|When unstructuring, lists are copied and their contents are handled according to their inner type.
177|A useful use case for unstructuring collections is to create a deep copy of a complex or recursive collection.
178|
179|```{versionchanged} 25.2.0
180|Sequences are no longer structured into lists by default, but tuples.
181|```
182|
183|### Dictionaries
184|
185|Dictionaries can be produced from other mapping objects.
186|More precisely, the unstructured object must expose an [`items()`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict.items) method producing an iterable of key-value tuples,
187|and be able to be passed to the `dict` constructor as an argument.
188|Types converting to dictionaries are:
189|
190|- `dict[K, V]` and `typing.Dict[K, V]`
191|- `collections.abc.MutableMapping[K, V]`
192|- `collections.abc.Mapping[K, V]`
193|
194|In all cases, a new dict will be returned, so this operation can be used to copy a mapping into a dict.
195|Any type parameters set to `typing.Any` will be passed through unconverted.
196|If both type parameters are absent, they will be treated as `Any` too.
197|
198|```{doctest}
199|
200|>>> from collections import OrderedDict
201|>>> cattrs.structure(OrderedDict([(1, 2), (3, 4)]), dict)
202|{1: 2, 3: 4}
203|```
204|
205|Both keys and values are converted.
206|
207|```{doctest}
208|
209|>>> cattrs.structure({1: None, 2: 2.0}, dict[str, Optional[int]])
210|{'1': None, '2': 2}
211|```
212|
213|### frozendicts
214|
215|On Python 3.15+, `frozendict` and `frozendict[K, V]` are supported.
216|Structuring produces a `frozendict`, converting keys and values according to the
217|type arguments when provided.
218|{class}`Converter <cattrs.Converter>` unstructures frozen dictionaries into plain
219|dictionaries, while {class}`BaseConverter <cattrs.BaseConverter>` preserves the
220|`frozendict` type.
221|`Mapping` unstructure collection overrides also apply to `frozendict`.
222|
223|### defaultdicts
224|
225|[`defaultdicts`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.html#collections.defaultdict)
226|can be structured by default if they can be initialized using their value type hint.
227|Supported types are:
228|
229|- `collections.defaultdict[K, V]`
230|- `typing.DefaultDict[K, V]`
231|
232|For example, `defaultdict[str, int]` works since _cattrs_ will initialize it with `defaultdict(int)`.
233|
234|This also means `defaultdicts` without key and value annotations (bare `defaultdicts`) cannot be structured by default.
235|
236|`defaultdicts` with arbitrary default factories can be structured by using {meth}`defaultdict_structure_factory <cattrs.cols.defaultdict_structure_factory>`:
237|
238|```{doctest}
239|>>> from collections import defaultdict
240|>>> from cattrs.cols import defaultdict_structure_factory
241|
242|>>> converter = Converter()
243|>>> hook = defaultdict_structure_factory(
244|...     defaultdict[str, int],
245|...     converter,
246|...     default_factory=lambda: 1
247|... )
248|
249|>>> hook({"key": 1})
250|defaultdict(<function <lambda> at ...>, {'key': 1})
251|```
252|
253|`defaultdicts` are unstructured into plain dictionaries.
254|
255|```{note}
256|`defaultdicts` are not supported by the BaseConverter.
257|```
258|
259|```{versionadded} 24.2.0
260|
261|```
262|
263|### Virtual Subclasses of [`abc.Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping) and [`abc.MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)
264|
265|If a class declares itself a virtual subclass of `collections.abc.Mapping` or `collections.abc.MutableMapping` and its initializer accepts a dictionary,
266|_cattrs_ will be able to structure it by default.
267|
268|### Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Tuples
269|
270|Homogeneous and heterogeneous tuples can be structured from iterable objects.
271|Heterogeneous tuples require an iterable with the number of elements matching the number of type parameters exactly.
272|
273|Heterogenous tuples use:
274|
275|- `typing.Tuple[A, B, C, D]`
276|- `tuple[A, B, C, D]`
277|
278|Homogeneous tuples use:
279|
280|- `collections.abc.Sequence[T]`
281|- `typing.Tuple[T, ...]`
282|- `tuple[T, ...]`
283|
284|In all cases a tuple will be produced.
285|Any type parameters set to `typing.Any` will be passed through unconverted.
286|
287|```{doctest}
288|
289|>>> cattrs.structure([1, 2, 3], tuple[int, str, float])
290|(1, '2', 3.0)
291|```
292|
293|When unstructuring, heterogeneous tuples unstructure into tuples since it's faster and virtually all serialization libraries support tuples natively.
294|
295|```{seealso}
296|[Support for typing.NamedTuple.](#typingnamedtuple)
297|```
298|
299|```{note}
300|Structuring heterogenous tuples are not supported by the BaseConverter.
301|```
302|
303|```{versionchanged} 25.2.0
304|Sequences are now structured into tuples.
305|```
306|
307|```{versionchanged} 26.2.0
308|The default {class}`Converter <cattrs.Converter>` now generates and caches specialized structuring hooks for heterogeneous tuples, improving repeated structuring performance.
309|```
310|
311|### Deques
312|
313|Deques can be structured from any iterable object.
314|Types converting to deques are:
315|
316|- `typing.Deque[T]`
317|- `collections.deque[T]`
318|
319|In all cases, a new **unbounded** deque (`maxlen=None`) will be produced, so this operation can be used to copy an iterable into a deque.
320|If you want to convert into bounded `deque`, registering a custom structuring hook is a good approach.
321|
322|```{doctest}
323|
324|>>> from collections import deque
325|>>> cattrs.structure((1, 2, 3), deque[int])
326|deque([1, 2, 3])
327|```
328|
329|Deques are unstructured into lists, or into deques when using the {class}`BaseConverter`.
330|
331|```{versionadded} 23.1.0
332|
333|```
334|
335|
336|### Sets and Frozensets
337|
338|Sets and frozensets can be structured from any iterable object.
339|Types converting to sets are:
340|
341|- `collections.abc.MutableSet[T]`
342|- `set[T]`
343|- `typing.Set[T]` (deprecated since Python 3.9, use `set[T]` instead)
344|
345|Types converting to frozensets are:
346|
347|- `collections.abc.Set[T]`
348|- `frozenset[T]`
349|- `typing.FrozenSet[T]` (deprecated since Python 3.9, use `frozenset[T]` instead)
350|
351|In all cases, a new set or frozenset will be returned.
352|A bare type, for example `MutableSet` instead of `MutableSet[int]`, is equivalent to `MutableSet[Any]`.
353|
354|```{doctest}
355|
356|>>> cattrs.structure([1, 2, 3, 4], set)
357|{1, 2, 3, 4}
358|```
359|
360|Sets and frozensets are unstructured into the matching class.
361|
362|```{versionchanged} 25.3.0
363|Abstract sets are now structured into frozensets instead of sets.
364|```
365|
366|### Typed Dicts
367|
368|[TypedDicts](https://peps.python.org/pep-0589/) can be structured from mapping objects, usually dictionaries.
369|
370|```{doctest}
371|>>> from typing import TypedDict
372|
373|>>> class MyTypedDict(TypedDict):
374|...    a: int
375|
376|>>> cattrs.structure({"a": "1"}, MyTypedDict)
377|{'a': 1}
378|```
379|
380|Both [_total_ and _non-total_](https://peps.python.org/pep-0589/#totality) TypedDicts are supported, and inheritance between any combination works.
381|Generic TypedDicts work on Python 3.11 and later, since that is the first Python version that supports them in general.
382|
383|[`typing.Required` and `typing.NotRequired`](https://peps.python.org/pep-0655/) are supported.
384|
385|:::{caution}
386|If `from __future__ import annotations` is used or if annotations are given as strings, `Required` and `NotRequired` are ignored by cattrs.
387|See [note in the Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.TypedDict.__optional_keys__).
388|:::
389|
390|[Similar to _attrs_ classes](customizing.md#using-cattrsgen-hook-factories), un/structuring can be customized using {meth}`cattrs.gen.typeddicts.make_dict_structure_fn` and {meth}`cattrs.gen.typeddicts.make_dict_unstructure_fn`.
391|
392|```{doctest}
393|>>> from typing import TypedDict
394|>>> from cattrs import Converter
395|>>> from cattrs.gen import override
396|>>> from cattrs.gen.typeddicts import make_dict_structure_fn
397|
398|>>> class MyTypedDict(TypedDict):
399|...     a: int
400|...     b: int
401|
402|>>> c = Converter()
403|>>> c.register_structure_hook(
404|...     MyTypedDict,
405|...     make_dict_structure_fn(
406|...         MyTypedDict,
407|...         c,
408|...         a=override(rename="a-with-dash")
409|...     )
410|... )
411|
412|>>> c.structure({"a-with-dash": 1, "b": 2}, MyTypedDict)
413|{'b': 2, 'a': 1}
414|```
415|
416|TypedDicts unstructure into dictionaries, potentially unchanged (depending on the exact field types and registered hooks).
417|
418|```{doctest}
419|>>> from typing import TypedDict
420|>>> from datetime import datetime, timezone
421|>>> from cattrs import Converter
422|
423|>>> class MyTypedDict(TypedDict):
424|...    a: datetime
425|
426|>>> c = Converter()
427|>>> c.register_unstructure_hook(datetime, lambda d: d.timestamp())
428|
429|>>> c.unstructure({"a": datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)}, unstructure_as=MyTypedDict)
430|{'a': 0.0}
431|```
432|
433|```{versionadded} 23.1.0
434|
435|```

437|
438|## _attrs_ Classes and Dataclasses
439|
440|_attrs_ classes and dataclasses work out of the box.
441|The fields require type annotations (even if static type-checking is not being used), or they will be treated as [](#typingany).
442|
443|When structuring, given a mapping `d` and class `A`, _cattrs_ will instantiate `A` with `d` unpacked.
444|
445|```{doctest}
446|
447|>>> @define
448|... class A:
449|...     a: int
450|...     b: int
451|
452|>>> cattrs.structure({'a': 1, 'b': '2'}, A)
453|A(a=1, b=2)
454|```
455|
456|Tuples can be structured into classes using {meth}`structure_attrs_fromtuple() <cattrs.structure_attrs_fromtuple>` (`fromtuple` as in the opposite of [`attrs.astuple`](https://www.attrs.org/en/stable/api.html#attrs.astuple) and {meth}`BaseConverter.unstructure_attrs_astuple`).
457|
458|```{doctest}
459|
460|>>> @define
461|... class A:
462|...     a: str
463|...     b: int
464|
465|>>> cattrs.structure_attrs_fromtuple(['string', '2'], A)
466|A(a='string', b=2)
467|```
468|
469|Loading from tuples can be made the default by creating a new {class}`Converter <cattrs.Converter>` with `unstruct_strat=cattrs.UnstructureStrategy.AS_TUPLE`.
470|
471|```{doctest}
472|
473|>>> converter = cattrs.Converter(unstruct_strat=cattrs.UnstructureStrategy.AS_TUPLE)
474|>>> @define
475|... class A:
476|...     a: str
477|...     b: int
478|
479|>>> converter.structure(['string', '2'], A)
480|A(a='string', b=2)
481|```
482|
483|Structuring from tuples can also be made the default for specific classes only by registering a hook the usual way.
484|
485|```{doctest}
486|
487|>>> converter = cattrs.Converter()
488|
489|>>> @define
490|... class A:
491|...     a: str
492|...     b: int
493|
494|>>> converter.register_structure_hook(A, converter.structure_attrs_fromtuple)
495|```
496|
497|
498|### Generics
499|
500|Generic _attrs_ classes and dataclasses are fully supported, both using `typing.Generic` and [PEP 695](https://peps.python.org/pep-0695/).
501|
502|```python
503|>>> @define
504|... class A[T]:
505|...    a: T
506|
507|>>> cattrs.structure({"a": "1"}, A[int])
508|A(a=1)
509|```
510|
511|
512|### Using Attribute Types and Converters
513|
514|By default, {meth}`structure() <cattrs.BaseConverter.structure>` will use hooks registered using {meth}`register_structure_hook() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_structure_hook>`
515|to convert values to the attribute type, and proceed to invoking any converters registered on attributes with `field`.
516|
517|```{doctest}
518|
519|>>> from ipaddress import IPv4Address, ip_address
520|>>> converter = cattrs.Converter()
521|
522|# Note: register_structure_hook has not been called, so this will fallback to 'ip_address'
523|>>> @define
524|... class A:
525|...     a: IPv4Address = field(converter=ip_address)
526|
527|>>> converter.structure({'a': '127.0.0.1'}, A)
528|A(a=IPv4Address('127.0.0.1'))
529|```
530|
531|Priority is still given to hooks registered with {meth}`register_structure_hook() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_structure_hook>`,
532|but this priority can be inverted by setting `prefer_attrib_converters` to `True`.
533|
534|```{doctest}
535|
536|>>> converter = cattrs.Converter(prefer_attrib_converters=True)
537|
538|>>> @define
539|... class A:
540|...     a: int = field(converter=lambda v: int(v) + 5)
541|
542|>>> converter.structure({'a': '10'}, A)
543|A(a=15)
544|```
545|
546|```{seealso}
547|If an _attrs_ or dataclass class uses inheritance and as such has one or several subclasses, it can be structured automatically to its exact subtype by using the [include subclasses](strategies.md#include-subclasses-strategy) strategy.
548|```
549|
550|
551|## Unions
552|
553|Unions of `NoneType` and a single other type (also known as optionals) are supported by a [special case](#optionals).
554|
555|
556|### Automatic Disambiguation
557|
558|_cattrs_ includes an opinionated strategy for automatically handling unions of _attrs_ classes; see [](unions.md#default-union-strategy) for details.
559|
560|When unstructuring these kinds of unions, each union member will be unstructured according to the hook for that type.
561|
562|
563|### Unions of Simple Types
564|
565|_cattrs_ comes with the [](strategies.md#union-passthrough), which enables converters to structure unions of many primitive types and literals.
566|This strategy can be applied to any converter, and is pre-applied to all [preconf](preconf.md) converters according to their underlying protocols.
567|
568|
569|## Special Typing Forms
570|
571|
572|### `typing.Any`
573|
574|When structuring, use `typing.Any` to avoid applying any conversions to the object you're structuring; it will simply be passed through.
575|
576|```{doctest}
577|
578|>>> cattrs.structure(1, Any)
579|1
580|>>> d = {1: 1}
581|>>> cattrs.structure(d, Any) is d
582|True
583|```
584|
585|When unstructuring, `typing.Any` will make the value be unstructured according to its runtime class.
586|
587|```{versionchanged} 24.1.0
588|Previously, the unstructuring rules for `Any` were underspecified, leading to inconsistent behavior.
589|```
590|
591|```{versionchanged} 24.1.0
592|`typing_extensions.Any` is now also supported.
593|```
594|
595|### Sentinels
596|
597|On Python 3.15+, built-in [`sentinel`](https://docs.python.org/3.15/builtins/functions.html#sentinel) values are unstructured to their names.
598|Structuring a matching name into a sentinel annotation restores that exact sentinel instance; other values raise a `CattrsError`.
599|
600|```{doctest}
601|:skipif: __import__("sys").version_info < (3, 15)
602|
603|>>> MISSING = sentinel("MISSING")
604|
605|>>> cattrs.unstructure(MISSING)
606|'MISSING'
607|>>> cattrs.structure("MISSING", MISSING) is MISSING
608|True
609|>>> cattrs.structure("MISSING", int | MISSING) is MISSING
610|True
611|>>> cattrs.structure("1", int | MISSING)
612|1
613|```
614|
615|In unions, sentinel names take precedence over the remaining members, including `str` and `Any`.
616|Sentinels in the same union must have distinct names.
617|The remaining members must form a type the converter supports.
618|Sentinel defaults work with the existing `omit_if_default` option; they are serialized normally unless that option is enabled.
619|
620|Hooks can be registered for individual sentinel instances using `register_structure_hook` and `register_unstructure_hook`.
621|If custom hooks change a sentinel's representation, register a hook for any containing union as well: the default union hook matches sentinel names.
622|
623|```{versionadded} NEXT
624|
625|```
626|
627|### `typing.Literal`
628|
629|When structuring, [PEP 586](https://peps.python.org/pep-0586/) literals are validated to be in the allowed set of values.
630|
631|```{doctest}
632|>>> from typing import Literal
633|
634|>>> cattrs.structure(1, Literal[1, 2])
635|1
636|```
637|
638|When unstructuring, literals are passed through.
639|
640|```{versionadded} 1.7.0
641|
642|```
643|
644|### `typing.NamedTuple`
645|
646|Named tuples with type hints (created from [`typing.NamedTuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.NamedTuple)) are supported.
647|Named tuples are un/structured using tuples or lists by default.
648|
649|The {mod}`cattrs.cols` module contains hook factories for un/structuring named tuples using dictionaries instead,
650|[see here for details](customizing.md#customizing-named-tuples).
651|
652|```{versionadded} 24.1.0
653|
654|```
655|
656|### `typing.Final`
657|
658|[PEP 591](https://peps.python.org/pep-0591/) Final attribute types (`Final[int]`) are supported and handled according to the inner type (in this case, `int`).
659|
660|```{versionadded} 23.1.0
661|
662|```
663|
664|
665|### `typing.Annotated`
666|
667|[PEP 593](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0593/) annotations (`typing.Annotated[type, ...]`) are supported and are handled using the first type present in the annotated type.
668|
669|Additionally, `typing.Annotated` types containing `cattrs.override()` are recognized and used by the _attrs_, dataclass, TypedDict and dict NamedTuple hook factories.
670|
671|```{versionchanged} 26.1.0
672|`Annotated[T, override()]` is now used by the _attrs_, dataclass, TypedDict and dict NamedTuple hook factories.
673|```
674|
675|```{versionadded} 1.4.0
676|
677|```
678|
679|
680|### Type Aliases
681|
682|[Type aliases](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#type-aliases) are supported on Python 3.12+ and are handled according to the rules for their underlying type.
683|Their hooks can also be overriden using [](customizing.md#predicate-hooks).
684|
685|```{warning}
686|Type aliases using [`typing.TypeAlias`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.TypeAlias) aren't supported since there is no way at runtime to distinguish them from their underlying types.
687|```
688|
689|```{versionchanged} 26.2.0
690|The [union passthrough strategy](strategies.md#union-passthrough) also recognizes type aliases used as union members.
691|```
692|
693|```python
694|>>> from datetime import datetime, UTC
695|
696|>>> type IsoDate = datetime
697|
698|>>> converter = cattrs.Converter()
699|>>> converter.register_structure_hook_func(
700|...     lambda t: t is IsoDate, lambda v, _: datetime.fromisoformat(v)
701|... )
702|>>> converter.register_unstructure_hook_func(
703|...     lambda t: t is IsoDate, lambda v: v.isoformat()
704|... )
705|
706|>>> converter.structure("2022-01-01", IsoDate)
707|datetime.datetime(2022, 1, 1, 0, 0)
708|>>> converter.unstructure(datetime.now(UTC), unstructure_as=IsoDate)
709|'2023-11-20T23:10:46.728394+00:00'
710|```
711|
712|```{versionadded} 24.1.0
713|
714|```
715|
716|
717|### `typing.NewType`
718|
719|[NewTypes](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#newtype) are supported and are handled according to the rules for their underlying type.
720|Their hooks can also be overriden using {meth}`Converter.register_structure_hook() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_structure_hook>`.
721|
722|```{doctest}
723|
724|>>> from typing import NewType
725|>>> from datetime import datetime
726|
727|>>> IsoDate = NewType("IsoDate", datetime)
728|
729|>>> converter = cattrs.Converter()
730|>>> converter.register_structure_hook(IsoDate, lambda v, _: datetime.fromisoformat(v))
731|
732|>>> converter.structure("2022-01-01", IsoDate)
733|datetime.datetime(2022, 1, 1, 0, 0)
734|```
735|
736|```{versionadded} 22.2.0
737|
738|```
739|
740|
741|### `typing.Protocol`
742|
743|[Protocols](https://peps.python.org/pep-0544/) cannot be structured by default and so require custom hooks.
744|
745|Protocols are unstructured according to the actual runtime type of the value.
746|
747|```{versionadded} 1.9.0
748|
749|```
750|
751|### `typing.Self`
752|
753|Attributes annotated using [the Self type](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Self) are supported in _attrs_ classes, dataclasses, TypedDicts and NamedTuples
754|(when using [the dict un/structure factories](customizing.md#customizing-named-tuples)).
755|
756|```{doctest}
757|>>> from typing import Self
758|
759|>>> @define
760|... class LinkedListNode:
761|...     element: int
762|...     next: Self | None = None
763|
764|>>> cattrs.unstructure(LinkedListNode(1, LinkedListNode(2, None)))
765|{'element': 1, 'next': {'element': 2, 'next': None}}
766|>>> cattrs.structure({'element': 1, 'next': {'element': 2, 'next': None}}, LinkedListNode)
767|LinkedListNode(element=1, next=LinkedListNode(element=2, next=None))
768|```
769|
770|```{note}
771|Attributes annotated with `typing.Self` are not supported by the BaseConverter, as this is too complex for it.
772|```
773|
774|```{versionadded} 25.1.0
775|
776|```

91|    * enums are passed through to msgspec directly

132|    converter.register_unstructure_hook_factory(is_sequence, seq_unstructure_factory)

135|    )

145|def seq_unstructure_factory(type, converter: Converter) -> UnstructureHook:
146|    """The msgspec unstructure hook factory for sequences."""
147|    if is_bare(type):
148|        type_arg = Any
149|    else:
150|        args = get_args(type)
151|        type_arg = args[0]
152|    handler = converter.get_unstructure_hook(type_arg, cache_result=False)
153|
154|    if handler in (identity, to_builtins):
155|        return handler
156|    return converter.gen_unstructure_iterable(type)

159|def mapping_unstructure_factory(type, converter: Converter) -> UnstructureHook:
160|    """The msgspec unstructure hook factory for mappings."""
161|    if frozendict is not None and is_subclass(get_origin(type) or type, frozendict):
162|        # msgspec cannot serialize frozen dictionaries directly.
163|        return converter.gen_unstructure_mapping(type)
164|    if is_bare(type):
165|        key_arg = Any
166|        val_arg = Any
167|        key_handler = converter.get_unstructure_hook(key_arg, cache_result=False)
168|        value_handler = converter.get_unstructure_hook(val_arg, cache_result=False)
169|    else:
170|        args = get_args(type)
171|        if len(args) == 2:
172|            key_arg, val_arg = args
173|        else:
174|            # Probably a Counter
175|            key_arg, val_arg = args, Any
176|        key_handler = converter.get_unstructure_hook(key_arg, cache_result=False)
177|        value_handler = converter.get_unstructure_hook(val_arg, cache_result=False)
178|
179|    if key_handler in (identity, to_builtins) and value_handler in (
180|        identity,
181|        to_builtins,
182|    ):
183|        return to_builtins
184|    return converter.gen_unstructure_mapping(type)

187|def msgspec_attrs_unstructure_factory(
188|    type: Any, converter: Converter, msgspec_skips_private: bool = True
189|) -> UnstructureHook:
190|    """Choose whether to use msgspec handling or our own.
191|
192|    Args:
193|        msgspec_skips_private: Whether the msgspec library skips unstructuring
194|            private attributes, making us do the work.
195|    """
196|    origin = get_origin(type)
197|    base = origin or type
198|    attribs = fields(base)
199|    if attrs_has(type) and any(isinstance(a.type, str) for a in attribs):
200|        resolve_types(type)
201|        attribs = fields(base)
202|
203|    if msgspec_skips_private and any(attr.name.startswith("_") for attr in attribs):
204|        # Private attributes we have to do ourselves.
205|        return _gen_attrs_hook(type, converter)
206|
207|    try:
208|        working_set = _already_probing.working_set
209|        if base in working_set:
210|            return to_builtins
211|    except AttributeError:
212|        working_set = set()
213|        _already_probing.working_set = working_set
214|
215|    try:
216|        working_set.add(base)
217|        needs_hook = any(
218|            converter.get_unstructure_hook(attr.type, cache_result=False)
219|            not in (identity, to_builtins)
220|            for attr in attribs
221|        )
222|    finally:
223|        working_set.remove(base)
224|        if not working_set:
225|            del _already_probing.working_set
226|
227|    return _gen_attrs_hook(type, converter) if needs_hook else to_builtins

230|def _gen_attrs_hook(type: Any, converter: Converter) -> UnstructureHook:
231|    """Generate the hook, deferring generation to the first call during a probe.
232|
233|    Hooks generated during a probe would bake in the `to_builtins` answers
234|    the probe gives for classes it is still visiting.
235|    """
236|    if not hasattr(_already_probing, "working_set"):
237|        return converter.gen_unstructure_attrs_fromdict(type)
238|
239|    hook = None
240|
241|    def unstructure_lazily(obj):
242|        nonlocal hook
243|        if hook is None:
244|            hook = converter.gen_unstructure_attrs_fromdict(type)
245|        return hook(obj)
246|
247|    return unstructure_lazily
248|
249|
250|def namedtuple_unstructure_factory(
251|    type: type[tuple], converter: BaseConverter
252|) -> UnstructureHook:
253|    """A hook factory for unstructuring namedtuples, modified for msgspec."""
254|
255|    if all(
256|        converter.get_unstructure_hook(t) in (identity, to_builtins)
257|        for t in get_type_hints(type).values()
258|    ):
259|        return identity
260|
261|    return make_hetero_tuple_unstructure_fn(
262|        type,
263|        converter,
264|        unstructure_to=tuple,
265|        type_args=tuple(get_type_hints(type).values()),
266|    )

1|# Customizing (Un-)structuring
2|
3|This section describes customizing the unstructuring and structuring processes in _cattrs_.
4|
5|As you go about customizing converters by registering hooks and hook factories,
6|keep in mind that **the order of hook registration matters**.
7|
8|Technically speaking, whether the order matters or not depends on the actual implementation of hook factories used.
9|In practice, the built-in _cattrs_ hooks are optimized to perform early resolution of hooks.
10|You will likely compose with these hook factories.
11|
12|This means that **hooks for simpler types should be registered first**.
13|For example, to override hooks for structuring `int` and `list[int]`, the hook for `int`
14|must be registered first.
15|When the {meth}`list_structure_factory() <cattrs.cols.list_structure_factory>`
16|is applied to the `list[int]` type to produce a hook, it will retrieve and store
17|the hook for `int`, which should be already present.
18|
19|## Custom (Un-)structuring Hooks
20|
21|You can write your own structuring and unstructuring functions and register them for types using {meth}`Converter.register_structure_hook() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_structure_hook>` and {meth}`Converter.register_unstructure_hook() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_unstructure_hook>`.
22|
23|{meth}`register_structure_hook() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_structure_hook>` and {meth}`register_unstructure_hook() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_unstructure_hook>` use a Python [_singledispatch_](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functools.html#functools.singledispatch) under the hood.
24|_singledispatch_ is powerful and fast but comes with some limitations; namely that it performs checks using `issubclass()` which doesn't work with many Python types.
25|Some examples of this are:
26|
27|- various generic collections (`list[int]` is not a _subclass_ of `list`)
28|- literals (`Literal[1]` is not a _subclass_ of `Literal[1]`)
29|- generics (`MyClass[int]` is not a _subclass_ of `MyClass`)
30|- protocols, unless they are `runtime_checkable`
31|- various modifiers, such as `Final` and `NotRequired`
32|- `typing.Annotated`
33|
34|... and many others. In these cases, [predicate hooks](#predicate-hooks) should be used instead.
35|
36|Even though unions, [newtypes](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#newtype)
37|and [modern type aliases](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#type-aliases)
38|do not work with _singledispatch_,
39|these methods have special support for these type forms and can be used with them.
40|Instead of using _singledispatch_, predicate hooks will automatically be used instead.
41|
42|### Use as Decorators
43|
44|{meth}`register_structure_hook() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_structure_hook>` and {meth}`register_unstructure_hook() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_unstructure_hook>` can also be used as _decorators_.
45|When used this way they behave a little differently.
46|
47|{meth}`register_structure_hook() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_structure_hook>` will inspect the return type of the hook and register the hook for that type.
48|
49|```python
50|@converter.register_structure_hook
51|def my_int_hook(val: Any, _) -> int:
52|    """This hook will be registered for `int`s."""
53|    return int(val)
54|```
55|
56|{meth}`register_unstructure_hook() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_unstructure_hook>` will inspect the type of the first argument and register the hook for that type.
57|
58|```python
59|from datetime import datetime
60|
61|@converter.register_unstructure_hook
62|def my_datetime_hook(val: datetime) -> str:
63|    """This hook will be registered for `datetime`s."""
64|    return val.isoformat()
65|```
66|
67|The non-decorator approach is still recommended when dealing with lambdas, hooks produced elsewhere, unannotated hooks and situations where type introspection doesn't work.
68|
69|```{versionadded} 24.1.0
70|
71|```
72|
73|### Predicate Hooks
74|
75|A _predicate_ is a function that takes a type and returns true or false
76|depending on whether the associated hook can handle the given type.
77|
78|The {meth}`register_unstructure_hook_func() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_unstructure_hook_func>` and {meth}`register_structure_hook_func() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_structure_hook_func>` are used
79|to link un/structuring hooks to arbitrary types. These hooks are then called _predicate hooks_, and are very powerful.
80|
81|Predicate hooks are evaluated after the _singledispatch_ hooks.
82|In the case where both a _singledispatch_ hook and a predicate hook are present, the _singledispatch_ hook will be used.
83|Predicate hooks are checked in reverse order of registration, one-by-one, until a match is found.
84|
85|The following example demonstrates a predicate that checks for the presence of an attribute on a class (`custom`), and then overrides the structuring logic.
86|
87|```{doctest}
88|
89|>>> class D:
90|...     custom = True
91|...     def __init__(self, a):
92|...         self.a = a
93|...     def __repr__(self):
94|...         return f'D(a={self.a})'
95|...     @classmethod
96|...     def deserialize(cls, data):
97|...         return cls(data["a"])
98|
99|>>> cattrs.register_structure_hook_func(
100|...     lambda cls: getattr(cls, "custom", False), lambda d, t: t.deserialize(d)
101|... )
102|
103|>>> cattrs.structure({'a': 2}, D)
104|D(a=2)
105|```
106|
107|### Hook Factories
108|
109|Hook factories are higher-order predicate hooks: they are functions that _produce_ hooks.
110|Hook factories are commonly used to create very optimized hooks by offloading part of the work into a separate, earlier step.
111|
112|Hook factories are registered using {meth}`Converter.register_unstructure_hook_factory() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_unstructure_hook_factory>` and {meth}`Converter.register_structure_hook_factory() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_structure_hook_factory>`.
113|
114|Here's an example showing how to use hook factories to apply the `forbid_extra_keys` to all attrs classes:
115|
116|```python
117|>>> from attrs import define, has
118|>>> from cattrs import Converter
119|>>> from cattrs.gen import make_dict_structure_fn
120|
121|>>> c = Converter()
122|
123|>>> c.register_structure_hook_factory(
124|...     has,
125|...     lambda cl: make_dict_structure_fn(cl, c, _cattrs_forbid_extra_keys=True)
126|... )
127|
128|>>> @define
129|... class E:
130|...    an_int: int
131|
132|>>> c.structure({"an_int": 1, "else": 2}, E)
133|Traceback (most recent call last):
134|...
135|cattrs.errors.ForbiddenExtraKeysError: Extra fields in constructor for E: else
136|```
137|
138|Hook factories can receive the current converter by exposing an additional required parameter.
139|
140|A complex use case for hook factories is described over at [](usage.md#using-factory-hooks).
141|
142|#### Use as Decorators
143|
144|{meth}`register_unstructure_hook_factory() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_unstructure_hook_factory>` and
145|{meth}`register_structure_hook_factory() <cattrs.BaseConverter.register_structure_hook_factory>` can also be used as decorators.
146|
147|Here's an example of using an unstructure hook factory to handle unstructuring [queues](https://docs.python.org/3/library/queue.html#queue.Queue).
148|
149|```{doctest}
150|>>> from collections.abc import Callable
151|>>> from queue import Queue
152|>>> from typing import Any, get_args, get_origin
153|>>> from cattrs import Converter
154|
155|>>> c = Converter()
156|
157|>>> @c.register_unstructure_hook_factory(lambda t: get_origin(t) is Queue)
158|... def queue_hook_factory(cl: Any, converter: Converter) -> Callable:
159|...     type_arg = get_args(cl)[0]
160|...     elem_handler = converter.get_unstructure_hook(type_arg)
161|...
162|...     def unstructure_hook(v: Queue) -> list:
163|...         res = []
164|...         while not v.empty():
165|...             res.append(elem_handler(v.get_nowait()))
166|...         return res
167|...
168|...     return unstructure_hook
169|
170|>>> q = Queue()
171|>>> q.put(1)
172|>>> q.put(2)
173|
174|>>> c.unstructure(q, unstructure_as=Queue[int])
175|[1, 2]
176|```
177|
178|## Using `cattrs.gen` Hook Factories
179|
180|The {mod}`cattrs.gen` module contains [hook factories](#hook-factories) for un/structuring _attrs_ classes, dataclasses and typed dicts.
181|The default {class}`Converter <cattrs.Converter>`, upon first encountering one of these types,
182|will use the hook factories mentioned here to generate specialized hooks for it,
183|register the hooks and use them.
184|
185|One reason for generating these hooks in advance is that they can bypass a lot of _cattrs_ machinery and be significantly faster than normal _cattrs_.
186|The hook factories are also good building blocks for more complex customizations.
187|
188|Another reason is overriding behavior on a per-attribute basis.
189|
190|Currently, the overrides only support generating dictionary un/structuring hooks (as opposed to tuples),
191|and support `omit_if_default`, `forbid_extra_keys`, `rename` and `omit`.
192|
193|### `omit_if_default`
194|```{currentmodule} cattrs.gen
195|```
196|
197|This override can be applied on a per-class or per-attribute basis.
198|The generated unstructuring hook will skip unstructuring values that are equal to their default or factory values.
199|By default, {func}`make_dict_unstructure_fn` and {func}`make_dict_unstructure_fn_from_attrs`
200|inherit the converter's `omit_if_default` setting (`False` for a {class}`cattrs.BaseConverter`).
201|Pass `_cattrs_omit_if_default=True` or `_cattrs_omit_if_default=False` to override this setting
202|for a particular hook; per-attribute overrides take precedence over either value.
203|
204|If a default-valued field is needed to select a class during structuring, such as a `Literal` discriminator, preserve it with `override(omit_if_default=False)`.
205|This also applies when using {func}`cattrs.strategies.include_subclasses` with `overrides`, since those generated hooks now inherit the converter setting.
206|For example, pass `overrides={"kind": override(omit_if_default=False)}` to keep a `kind` discriminator while omitting other default-valued fields.
207|
208|```{doctest}
209|
210|>>> from cattrs.gen import make_dict_unstructure_fn, override
211|
212|>>> @define
213|... class WithDefault:
214|...    a: int
215|...    b: dict = Factory(dict)
216|
217|>>> c = cattrs.Converter()
218|>>> c.register_unstructure_hook(
219|...     WithDefault, 
220|...     make_dict_unstructure_fn(WithDefault, c, b=override(omit_if_default=True)),
221|... )
222|>>> c.unstructure(WithDefault(1))
223|{'a': 1}
224|```
225|
226|Note that the per-attribute value overrides the per-class value.
227|A side-effect of this is the ability to force the presence of a subset of fields.
228|For example, consider a class with a `dateTime` field and a factory for it: skipping the unstructuring of the `dateTime` field would be inconsistent and based on the current time.
229|So we apply the `omit_if_default` rule to the class, but not to the `dateTime` field.
230|
231|```{note}
232|The parameter to {meth}`make_dict_unstructure_fn` is named ``_cattrs_omit_if_default`` instead of just ``omit_if_default`` to avoid potential collisions with an override for a field named ``omit_if_default``.
233|```
234|
235|```{doctest}
236|
237|>>> from datetime import datetime
238|>>> from cattrs.gen import make_dict_unstructure_fn, override
239|
240|>>> @define
241|... class TestClass:
242|...     a: int | None = None
243|...     b: datetime = Factory(datetime.utcnow)
244|
245|>>> c = cattrs.Converter()
246|>>> hook = make_dict_unstructure_fn(
247|...     TestClass, 
248|...     c,
249|...     _cattrs_omit_if_default=True, 
250|...     b=override(omit_if_default=False)
251|... )
252|>>> c.register_unstructure_hook(TestClass, hook)
253|>>> c.unstructure(TestClass())
254|{'b': ...}
255|```
256|
257|This override has no effect when generating structuring functions.
258|
259|### `forbid_extra_keys`
260|
261|By default _cattrs_ is lenient in accepting unstructured input.
262|If extra keys are present in a dictionary, they will be ignored when generating a structured object.
263|Sometimes it may be desirable to enforce a stricter contract, and to raise an error when unknown keys are present - in particular when fields have default values this may help with catching typos.
264|`forbid_extra_keys` can also be enabled (or disabled) on a per-class basis when creating structure hooks with {meth}`make_dict_structure_fn() <cattrs.gen.make_dict_structure_fn>`.
265|
266|```{doctest}
267|    :options: +SKIP
268|
269|>>> from cattrs.gen import make_dict_structure_fn
270|>>>
271|>>> @define
272|... class TestClass:
273|...    number: int = 1
274|>>>
275|>>> c = cattrs.Converter(forbid_extra_keys=True)
276|>>> c.structure({"nummber": 2}, TestClass)
277|Traceback (most recent call last):
278|...
279|ForbiddenExtraKeyError: Extra fields in constructor for TestClass: nummber
280|>>> hook = make_dict_structure_fn(TestClass, c, _cattrs_forbid_extra_keys=False)
281|>>> c.register_structure_hook(TestClass, hook)
282|>>> c.structure({"nummber": 2}, TestClass)
283|TestClass(number=1)
284|```
285|
286|This behavior can only be applied to classes or to the default for the {class}`Converter <cattrs.Converter>`, and has no effect when generating unstructuring functions.
287|
288|```{versionchanged} 23.2.0
289|The value for the `make_dict_structure_fn._cattrs_forbid_extra_keys` parameter is now taken from the given converter by default.
290|```
291|
292|### `rename`
293|
294|Using the rename override makes `cattrs` use the provided name instead of the real attribute name.
295|This is useful if an attribute name is a reserved keyword in Python.
296|
297|```{doctest}
298|
299|>>> from pendulum import DateTime
300|>>> from cattrs.gen import make_dict_unstructure_fn, make_dict_structure_fn, override
301|
302|>>> @define
303|... class ExampleClass:
304|...     klass: int | None
305|
306|>>> c = cattrs.Converter()
307|>>> unst_hook = make_dict_unstructure_fn(ExampleClass, c, klass=override(rename="class"))
308|>>> st_hook = make_dict_structure_fn(ExampleClass, c, klass=override(rename="class"))
309|>>> c.register_unstructure_hook(ExampleClass, unst_hook)
310|>>> c.register_structure_hook(ExampleClass, st_hook)
311|>>> c.unstructure(ExampleClass(1))
312|{'class': 1}
313|>>> c.structure({'class': 1}, ExampleClass)
314|ExampleClass(klass=1)
315|```
316|
317|### `omit`
318|
319|This override can only be applied to individual attributes.
320|Using the `omit` override will simply skip the attribute completely when generating a structuring or unstructuring function.
321|
322|```{doctest}
323|
324|>>> from cattrs.gen import make_dict_unstructure_fn, override
325|>>>
326|>>> @define
327|... class ExampleClass:
328|...     an_int: int
329|>>>
330|>>> c = cattrs.Converter()
331|>>> unst_hook = make_dict_unstructure_fn(ExampleClass, c, an_int=override(omit=True))
332|>>> c.register_unstructure_hook(ExampleClass, unst_hook)
333|>>> c.unstructure(ExampleClass(1))
334|{}
335|```
336|
337|### `struct_hook` and `unstruct_hook`
338|
339|By default, the generators will determine the right un/structure hook for each attribute of a class at time of generation according to the type of each individual attribute.
340|
341|This process can be overriden by passing in the desired un/structure hook manually.
342|
343|```{doctest}
344|
345|>>> from cattrs.gen import make_dict_structure_fn, override
346|
347|>>> @define
348|... class ExampleClass:
349|...     an_int: int
350|
351|>>> c = cattrs.Converter()
352|>>> st_hook = make_dict_structure_fn(
353|...     ExampleClass, c, an_int=override(struct_hook=lambda v, _: v + 1)
354|... )
355|>>> c.register_structure_hook(ExampleClass, st_hook)
356|
357|>>> c.structure({"an_int": 1}, ExampleClass)
358|ExampleClass(an_int=2)
359|```
360|
361|### `use_alias`
362|
363|By default, fields are un/structured to and from dictionary keys exactly matching the field names.
364|_attrs_ classes support _attrs_ field aliases, which override the `__init__` parameter name for a given field.
365|By generating your un/structure function with `_cattrs_use_alias=True`, _cattrs_ will use the field alias instead of the field name as the un/structured dictionary key.
366|
367|```{doctest}
368|
369|>>> from cattrs.gen import make_dict_structure_fn
370|>>>
371|>>> @define
372|... class AliasClass:
373|...    number: int = field(default=1, alias="count")
374|>>>
375|>>> c = cattrs.Converter()
376|>>> hook = make_dict_structure_fn(AliasClass, c, _cattrs_use_alias=True)
377|>>> c.register_structure_hook(AliasClass, hook)
378|>>> c.structure({"count": 2}, AliasClass)
379|AliasClass(number=2)
380|```
381|
382|```{versionadded} 23.2.0
383|
384|```
385|
386|### `include_init_false`
387|
388|By default, _attrs_ fields defined as `init=False` are skipped when un/structuring.
389|By generating your un/structure function with `_cattrs_include_init_false=True`, all `init=False` fields will be included for un/structuring.
390|
391|```{doctest}
392|
393|>>> from cattrs.gen import make_dict_structure_fn
394|>>>
395|>>> @define
396|... class ClassWithInitFalse:
397|...    number: int = field(default=1, init=False)
398|>>>
399|>>> c = cattrs.Converter()
400|>>> hook = make_dict_structure_fn(ClassWithInitFalse, c, _cattrs_include_init_false=True)
401|>>> c.register_structure_hook(ClassWithInitFalse, hook)
402|>>> c.structure({"number": 2}, ClassWithInitFalse)
403|ClassWithInitFalse(number=2)
404|```
405|
406|A single attribute can be included by overriding it with `omit=False`.
407|
408|```{doctest}
409|
410|>>> c = cattrs.Converter()
411|>>> hook = make_dict_structure_fn(ClassWithInitFalse, c, number=override(omit=False))
412|>>> c.register_structure_hook(ClassWithInitFalse, hook)
413|>>> c.structure({"number": 2}, ClassWithInitFalse)
414|ClassWithInitFalse(number=2)
415|```
416|
417|```{versionadded} 23.2.0
418|
419|```
420|
421|## Using `typing.Annotated[T, override(...)]`
422|
423|The un/structuring process for _attrs_ classes, dataclasses, TypedDicts and dict NamedTuples can be customized by annotating the fields using `typing.Annotated[T, override()]`.
424|
425|```{doctest}
426|>>> from typing import Annotated
427|
428|>>> @define
429|... class ExampleClass:
430|...     klass: Annotated[int, cattrs.override(rename="class")]
431|
432|>>> cattrs.unstructure(ExampleClass(1))
433|{'class': 1}
434|>>> cattrs.structure({'class': 1}, ExampleClass)
435|ExampleClass(klass=1)
436|```
437|
438|These customizations are automatically recognized by every {class}`Converter <cattrs.Converter>`.
439|They can still be overriden explicitly, see [](#custom-un-structuring-hooks).
440|
441|```{attention}
442|One of the fundamental [design decisions](why.md#design-decisions) of _cattrs_ is that serialization rules should be separate from the models themselves;
443|by using this feature you're going against the spirit of this design decision.
444|
445|However, software is written in many different context and with different constraints; and practicality _sometimes_ beats purity.
446|_Sometimes_, it's not worth introducing a mapping layer to rename one field.
447|_Sometimes_, you're busy prototyping and will clean up your code later.
448|
449|The danger is not any single compromise, but their accumulation.
450|One of the most important skills as a software engineer is knowing when the cost of a trade-off has crossed the line and it's time to do things properly.
451|```
452|
453|```{versionadded} 26.1.0
454|
455|```
456|
457|## Customizing Collections
458|
459|```{currentmodule} cattrs.cols
460|
461|```
462|
463|The {mod}`cattrs.cols` module contains predicates and hook factories useful for customizing collection handling.
464|These hook factories can be wrapped to apply complex customizations.
465|
466|Available predicates are:
467|
468|- {meth}`is_any_set`
469|- {meth}`is_frozenset`
470|- {meth}`is_set`
471|- {meth}`is_mutable_sequence`
472|- {meth}`is_sequence`
473|- {meth}`is_mapping`
474|- {meth}`is_namedtuple`
475|- {meth}`is_defaultdict`
476|
477|````{tip}
478|These predicates aren't _cattrs_-specific and may be useful in other contexts.
479|```{doctest} predicates
480|>>> from cattrs.cols import is_sequence
481|
482|>>> is_sequence(list[str])
483|True
484|```
485|````
486|
487|Available hook factories are:
488|
489|- {meth}`iterable_unstructure_factory`
490|- {meth}`list_structure_factory`
491|- {meth}`homogenous_tuple_structure_factory`
492|- {meth}`namedtuple_structure_factory`
493|- {meth}`namedtuple_unstructure_factory`
494|- {meth}`namedtuple_dict_structure_factory`
495|- {meth}`namedtuple_dict_unstructure_factory`
496|- {meth}`mapping_structure_factory`
497|- {meth}`mapping_unstructure_factory`
498|- {meth}`defaultdict_structure_factory`
499|
500|Additional predicates and hook factories will be added as requested.
501|
502|For example, by default mutable sequences are structured from any iterable into lists.
503|This may be too lax, and additional validation may be applied by wrapping the default list structuring hook factory.
504|
505|```{testcode} list-customization
506|from cattrs.cols import is_mutable_sequence, list_structure_factory
507|
508|c = Converter()
509|
510|@c.register_structure_hook_factory(is_mutable_sequence)
511|def strict_list_hook_factory(type, converter):
512|
513|    # First, we generate the default hook...
514|    list_hook = list_structure_factory(type, converter)
515|
516|    # Then, we wrap it with a function of our own...
517|    def strict_list_hook(value, type):
518|        if not isinstance(value, list):
519|            raise ValueError("Not a list!")
520|        return list_hook(value, type)
521|
522|    # And finally, we return our own composite hook.
523|    return strict_list_hook
524|```
525|
526|Now, all mutable sequence structuring will be stricter:
527|
528|```{doctest} list-customization
529|>>> c.structure({"a", "b", "c"}, list[str])
530|Traceback (most recent call last):
531|    ...
532|ValueError: Not a list!
533|```
534|
535|```{versionadded} 24.1.0
536|
537|```
538|```{versionchanged} 25.2.0
539|Added the {meth}`is_mutable_sequence` predicate and {meth}`homogenous_tuple_structure_factory` hook factory.
540|```
541|
542|### Customizing Named Tuples
543|
544|Named tuples can be un/structured using dictionaries using the {meth}`namedtuple_dict_structure_factory`
545|and {meth}`namedtuple_dict_unstructure_factory` hook factories.
546|
547|To unstructure _all_ named tuples into dictionaries:
548|
549|```{doctest} namedtuples
550|>>> from typing import NamedTuple
551|
552|>>> from cattrs.cols import is_namedtuple, namedtuple_dict_unstructure_factory
553|>>> c = Converter()
554|
555|>>> c.register_unstructure_hook_factory(is_namedtuple, namedtuple_dict_unstructure_factory)
556|<function namedtuple_dict_unstructure_factory at ...>
557|
558|>>> class MyNamedTuple(NamedTuple):
559|...     a: int
560|
561|>>> c.unstructure(MyNamedTuple(1))
562|{'a': 1}
563|```
564|
565|To only un/structure _some_ named tuples into dictionaries,
566|change the predicate function when registering the hook factory:
567|
568|```{doctest} namedtuples
569|    :options: +ELLIPSIS
570|

1|# Strategies
2|
3|_cattrs_ ships with a number of _strategies_ for customizing un/structuring behavior.
4|
5|Strategies are prepackaged, high-level patterns for quickly and easily applying complex customizations to a converter.
6|
7|## Tagged Unions Strategy
8|
9|_Found at {py:func}`cattrs.strategies.configure_tagged_union`._
10|
11|The _tagged union_ strategy allows for un/structuring a union of classes by including an additional field (the _tag_) in the unstructured representation.
12|Each tag value is associated with a member of the union.
13|
14|```{doctest} tagged_unions
15|
16|>>> from cattrs.strategies import configure_tagged_union
17|>>> from cattrs import Converter
18|>>> converter = Converter()
19|
20|>>> @define
21|... class A:
22|...     a: int
23|
24|>>> @define
25|... class B:
26|...     b: str
27|
28|>>> configure_tagged_union(A | B, converter)
29|
30|>>> converter.unstructure(A(1), unstructure_as=A | B)
31|{'a': 1, '_type': 'A'}
32|
33|>>> converter.structure({'a': 1, '_type': 'A'}, A | B)
34|A(a=1)
35|```
36|
37|By default, the tag field name is `_type` and the tag value is the class name of the union member.
38|Both the field name and value can be overriden.
39|
40|The `tag_generator` parameter is a one-argument callable that will be called with every member of the union to generate a mapping of tag values to union members.
41|Here are some common `tag_generator` uses:
42|
43|| Tag info available in         | Recommended `tag_generator`                             |
44|| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
45|| Name of the class             | Use the default, or `lambda cl: cl.__name__`            |
46|| A class variable (`classvar`) | `lambda cl: cl.classvar`                                |
47|| A dictionary (`mydict`)       | `mydict.get` or `mydict.__getitem__`                    |
48|| An enum of possible values    | Build a dictionary of classes to enum values and use it |
49|
50|The union members aren't required to be attrs classes or dataclasses, although those work automatically.
51|They may be anything that cattrs can un/structure from/to a dictionary, for example a type with registered custom hooks.
52|
53|A default member can be specified to be used if the tag is missing or is unknown.
54|This is useful for evolving APIs in a backwards-compatible way; an endpoint taking class `A` can be changed to take `A | B` with `A` as the default (for old clients which do not send the tag).
55|
56|This strategy only applies in the context of the union; the normal un/structuring hooks are left untouched.
57|This also means union members can be reused in multiple unions easily.
58|
59|```{doctest} tagged_unions
60|
61|# Unstructuring as a union.
62|>>> converter.unstructure(A(1), unstructure_as=A | B)
63|{'a': 1, '_type': 'A'}
64|
65|# Unstructuring as just an `A`.
66|>>> converter.unstructure(A(1))
67|{'a': 1}
68|```
69|
70|```{versionchanged} 25.1.0
71|The strategy can also be called with a type alias of a union.
72|```
73|
74|### Real-life Case Study
75|
76|The Apple App Store supports [server callbacks](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreservernotifications), by which Apple sends a JSON payload to a URL of your choice.
77|The payload can be interpreted as about a dozen different messages, based on the value of the `notificationType` field.
78|
79|To keep the example simple we define two classes, one for the `REFUND` event and one for everything else.
80|
81|```{testcode} apple
82|
83|@define
84|class Refund:
85|    originalTransactionId: str
86|
87|@define
88|class OtherAppleNotification:
89|    notificationType: str
90|
91|AppleNotification = Refund | OtherAppleNotification
92|
93|```
94|
95|Next, we use the _tagged unions_ strategy to prepare our converter.
96|The tag value for the `Refund` event is `REFUND`, and we can let the `OtherAppleNotification` class handle all the other cases.
97|The `tag_generator` parameter is a callable, so we can give it the `get` method of a dictionary.
98|
99|```{doctest} apple
100|
101|>>> from cattrs.strategies import configure_tagged_union
102|
103|>>> c = Converter()
104|>>> configure_tagged_union(
105|...     AppleNotification,
106|...     c,
107|...     tag_name="notificationType",
108|...     tag_generator={Refund: "REFUND"}.get,
109|...     default=OtherAppleNotification
110|... )
111|
112|```
113|
114|The converter is now ready to start structuring Apple notifications.
115|
116|```{doctest} apple
117|
118|>>> payload = {"notificationType": "REFUND", "originalTransactionId": "1"}
119|>>> notification = c.structure(payload, AppleNotification)
120|
121|>>> match notification:
122|...     case Refund(txn_id):
123|...         print(f"Refund for {txn_id}!")
124|...     case OtherAppleNotification(not_type):
125|...         print("Can't handle this yet")
126|Refund for 1!
127|```
128|
129|```{versionadded} 23.1.0
130|
131|```
132|
133|## Include Subclasses Strategy
134|
135|_Found at {py:func}`cattrs.strategies.include_subclasses`._
136|
137|The _include subclass_ strategy allows the un/structuring of a base class to an instance of itself or one of its descendants.
138|Conceptually with this strategy, each time an un/structure operation for the base class is asked, `cattrs` machinery replaces that operation as if the union of the base class and its descendants had been asked instead.
139|
140|```{doctest} include_subclass
141|
142|>>> from attrs import define
143|>>> from cattrs.strategies import include_subclasses
144|>>> from cattrs import Converter
145|
146|>>> @define
147|... class Parent:
148|...     a: int
149|
150|>>> @define
151|... class Child(Parent):
152|...     b: str
153|
154|>>> converter = Converter()
155|>>> include_subclasses(Parent, converter)
156|
157|>>> converter.unstructure(Child(a=1, b="foo"), unstructure_as=Parent)
158|{'a': 1, 'b': 'foo'}
159|
160|>>> converter.structure({'a': 1, 'b': 'foo'}, Parent)
161|Child(a=1, b='foo')
162|```
163|
164|In the example above, we asked to unstructure then structure a `Child` instance as the `Parent` class and in both cases we correctly obtained back the unstructured and structured versions of the `Child` instance.
165|If we did not apply the `include_subclasses` strategy, this is what we would have obtained:
166|
167|```python
168|>>> converter_no_subclasses = Converter()
169|
170|>>> converter_no_subclasses.unstructure(Child(a=1, b="foo"), unstructure_as=Parent)
171|{'a': 1}
172|
173|>>> converter_no_subclasses.structure({'a': 1, 'b': 'foo'}, Parent)
174|Parent(a=1)
175|```
176|
177|Without the application of the strategy, in both unstructure and structure operations, we received a `Parent` instance.
178|
179|```{note}
180|The handling of subclasses is an opt-in feature for two main reasons:
181|- Performance. While small and probably negligible in most cases the subclass handling incurs more function calls and has a performance impact.
182|- Customization. The specific handling of subclasses can be different from one situation to the other. In particular there is not apparent universal good defaults for disambiguating the union type. Consequently the decision is left to the user.
183|```
184|
185|```{warning}
186|To work properly, all subclasses must be defined when the `include_subclasses` strategy is applied to a `converter`. If subclasses types are defined later, for instance in the context of a plug-in mechanism using inheritance, then those late defined subclasses will not be part of the subclasses union type and will not be un/structured as expected.
187|```
188|
189|### Customization
190|
191|In the example shown in the previous section, the default options for `include_subclasses` work well because the `Child` class has an attribute that do not exist in the `Parent` class (the `b` attribute).
192|The automatic union type disambiguation function which is based on finding unique fields for each type of the union works as intended.
193|
194|Sometimes, more disambiguation customization is required.
195|For instance, the unstructuring operation would have failed if `Child` did not have an extra attribute or if a sibling of `Child` had also a `b` attribute.
196|For those cases, a callable of 2 positional arguments (a union type and a converter) defining a [tagged union strategy](strategies.md#tagged-unions-strategy) can be passed to the `include_subclasses` strategy.
197|{py:func}`configure_tagged_union()<cattrs.strategies.configure_tagged_union>` can be used as-is, but if you want to change its defaults, the [partial](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functools.html#functools.partial) function from the `functools` module in the standard library can come in handy.
198|
199|```python
200|
201|>>> from functools import partial
202|>>> from attrs import define
203|>>> from cattrs.strategies import include_subclasses, configure_tagged_union
204|>>> from cattrs import Converter
205|
206|>>> @define
207|... class Parent:
208|...     a: int
209|
210|>>> @define
211|... class Child1(Parent):
212|...     b: str
213|
214|>>> @define
215|... class Child2(Parent):
216|...     b: int
217|
218|>>> converter = Converter()
219|>>> union_strategy = partial(configure_tagged_union, tag_name="type_name")
220|>>> include_subclasses(Parent, converter, union_strategy=union_strategy)
221|
222|>>> converter.unstructure(Child1(a=1, b="foo"), unstructure_as=Parent)
223|{'a': 1, 'b': 'foo', 'type_name': 'Child1'}
224|
225|>>> converter.structure({'a': 1, 'b': 1, 'type_name': 'Child2'}, Parent)
226|Child2(a=1, b=1)
227|```
228|
229|Other customizations available see are (see {py:func}`include_subclasses()<cattrs.strategies.include_subclasses>`):
230|
231|- The exact list of subclasses that should participate to the union with the `subclasses` argument.
232|- Attribute overrides that permit the customization of attributes un/structuring like renaming an attribute.
233|
234|Here is an example involving both customizations:
235|
236|```python
237|
238|>>> from attrs import define
239|>>> from cattrs.strategies import include_subclasses
240|>>> from cattrs import Converter, override
241|
242|>>> @define
243|... class Parent:
244|...     a: int
245|
246|>>> @define
247|... class Child(Parent):
248|...     b: str
249|
250|>>> converter = Converter()
251|>>> include_subclasses(
252|...     Parent,
253|...     converter,
254|...     subclasses=(Parent, Child),
255|...     overrides={"b": override(rename="c")}
256|... )
257|
258|>>> converter.unstructure(Child(a=1, b="foo"), unstructure_as=Parent)
259|{'a': 1, 'c': 'foo'}
260|
261|>>> converter.structure({'a': 1, 'c': 'foo'}, Parent)
262|Child(a=1, b='foo')
263|```
264|
265|```{versionadded} 23.1.0
266|
267|```

269|## Using Class-Specific Structure and Unstructure Methods
270|
271|_Found at {py:func}`cattrs.strategies.use_class_methods`._
272|
273|This strategy allows for un/structuring logic on the models themselves.
274|It can be applied for both structuring and unstructuring (also simultaneously).
275|
276|If a class requires special handling for (un)structuring, you can add a dedicated (un)structuring
277|method:
278|
279|```{doctest} class_methods
280|
281|>>> from attrs import define
282|>>> from cattrs import Converter
283|>>> from cattrs.strategies import use_class_methods
284|
285|>>> @define
286|... class MyClass:
287|...     a: int
288|...
289|...     @classmethod
290|...     def _structure(cls, data: dict):
291|...         return cls(data["b"] + 1)  # expecting "b", not "a"
292|...
293|...     def _unstructure(self):
294|...         return {"c": self.a - 1}  # unstructuring as "c", not "a"
295|
296|>>> converter = Converter()
297|>>> use_class_methods(converter, "_structure", "_unstructure")
298|>>> print(converter.structure({"b": 42}, MyClass))
299|MyClass(a=43)
300|>>> print(converter.unstructure(MyClass(42)))
301|{'c': 41}
302|```
303|
304|Any class without a `_structure` or `_unstructure` method will use the default strategy for structuring or unstructuring, respectively.
305|Feel free to use other names.
306|The stategy can be applied multiple times (with different method names).
307|
308|If you want to (un)structured nested objects, just append a converter parameter to your (un)structuring methods and you will receive the converter there:
309|
310|```{doctest} class_methods
311|
312|>>> @define
313|... class Nested:
314|...     m: MyClass
315|...
316|...     @classmethod
317|...     def _structure(cls, data: dict, conv):
318|...         return cls(conv.structure(data["n"], MyClass))
319|...
320|...     def _unstructure(self, conv):
321|...         return {"n": conv.unstructure(self.m)}
322|
323|>>> print(converter.structure({"n": {"b": 42}}, Nested))
324|Nested(m=MyClass(a=43))
325|>>> print(converter.unstructure(Nested(MyClass(42))))
326|{'n': {'c': 41}}
327|```
328|
329|```{versionadded} 23.2.0
330|
331|```
